name: Strategic Finance & Growth Advisory
tagline: An advisory offering that helps healthcare leaders decide which growth investments to pursue, and how to fund and sequence them.
need:
New facilities, service lines, programs and market entries compete for limited capital and executive attention, and they are often advanced on enthusiasm rather than a clear financial picture. Boards, investors and government sponsors need to know whether an initiative is viable, which opportunities to pursue first, and how an approved plan will be funded and sequenced over several years.
This offering sits in the Plan stage of the Cleveland Clinic Healthcare Financial Advisory Lifecycle, which follows an organization's financial decisions through five stages: Plan, Measure, Optimize, Manage and Transform. The Plan stage covers deciding whether and how to invest, and answers the client question "Can we do this?" It is typically requested by new market entrants and organizations pursuing growth initiatives, new facilities or service line expansion. Scope ranges from a single business case to a full growth agenda.
value:
This offering is delivered by Cleveland Clinic's Finance Advisory team. Cleveland Clinic is an operating health system with 23 hospitals, 300 outpatient locations and about 83,000 caregivers, and has grown from Northeast Ohio into Florida, Las Vegas, Toronto, London and Abu Dhabi (figures as of December 31, 2025).
Clients get business cases built and challenged against Cleveland Clinic's own experience planning, funding and opening new services, programs and facilities, in established and new markets. Volume ramps, staffing, reimbursement and capital needs reflect how hospitals actually run rather than desk-based assumptions.
Models are built with the client's finance team, every assumption is documented, and the work is handed over with a walk-through so the team can update it as plans change.
deliverables: Market assessment: written report and Excel-based demand model forecasting volumes by service, with the population, utilization and market share assumptions behind each forecast
Feasibility assessment: written report on operational and financial viability, with the key risks and the conditions that must be met for success

Business case and pro forma: Excel-based financial model over a multi-year horizon set at scoping, showing return on investment (ROI), net present value (NPV) and internal rate of return (IRR) under best, base and downside scenarios, with sensitivity analysis on the assumptions that most affect the result
Service line or new program analysis: Excel-based model of volume, revenue, cost and staffing for each program evaluated
Investment prioritization matrix: Excel-based scoring tool that ranks growth opportunities on agreed strategic and financial criteria, reusable for future decisions
Implementation roadmap: phased, multi-year plan with milestones, dependencies, owners and the funding required each year
Executive presentation: findings and a go or no-go recommendation for each opportunity, prepared for the board or investment committee
deliveryDetail: Delivered by Cleveland Clinic's Finance Advisory team, working alongside the client's finance lead. The engagement opens with a virtual kickoff and a structured data request, followed by interviews with key stakeholders. Analysis and modeling take place in weekly virtual working sessions, where interim findings are reviewed with the client team. It closes with an executive readout, on-site or virtual, and a handover of the models.

Health systems are increasingly approached with, or are actively pursuing, partnerships, affiliations, joint ventures and acquisitions. Their economics depend heavily on structure, contribution levels, governance and how returns are shared, and material risks are not always visible in summary materials. Leadership needs an objective view of what a proposed arrangement would cost, return and risk before committing capital, brand or clinical capacity.

name: Financial Performance Improvement & Profitability
tagline: An advisory offering that shows leaders where margin is being lost, sizes the opportunities to recover it, and builds the cost foundations to see profitability by service line.
category: Finance Advisory: Measure and Optimize Stages
need:
Boards and executives facing margin pressure from rising labor, supply and operating costs need an objective view of where performance is falling short and why. Many organizations lack reliable benchmarks, consistent productivity measures or the cost accounting needed to know which procedures, patients and service lines generate or consume margin once direct and indirect costs are fully considered.
This offering spans the Measure and Optimize stages of the Cleveland Clinic Healthcare Financial Advisory Lifecycle, which follows an organization's financial decisions through five stages: Plan, Measure, Optimize, Manage and Transform. These stages cover understanding current financial performance and improving margin toward best-in-class, and answer the client questions "How are we performing?" and "How do we become best-in-class?" It is typically requested by organizations facing margin pressure, from growing providers with limited performance data to mature health systems pursuing sustained margin improvement.

Clients get an operator's view of margin. Cleveland Clinic balances financial sustainability with clinical quality across a large system, so opportunities are tested for what is achievable without compromising care, and the cost accounting foundations are those a working health system uses to manage service line performance.

name: Financial Reporting & Performance Management
tagline: An advisory offering that gives leaders consistent KPIs, trusted dashboards and a faster, repeatable month-end reporting process.
need:
Executives frequently receive financial information that is late, fragmented across systems or too detailed to act on. Without agreed definitions, the same key performance indicator (KPI) is calculated differently across hospitals and departments, dashboards built by different teams conflict, and month-end reporting depends on manual workarounds and the knowledge of a few individuals. Leadership needs consistent measures, a clear performance story each period and a realistic path to automation.
This offering sits in the Measure stage of the Cleveland Clinic Healthcare Financial Advisory Lifecycle, which follows an organization's financial decisions through five stages: Plan, Measure, Optimize, Manage and Transform. The Measure stage covers understanding how the organization is performing financially and why, and answers the client question "How are we performing?" It is typically requested by growing organizations and those with limited reporting capabilities or multiple, disconnected data sources.

name: Integrated Financial Planning, Forecasting & Modeling
tagline: An advisory offering that helps finance teams build driver-based plans, budgets and forecasts that connect volumes, staffing, revenue and capital.
need:
Volume assumptions drive nearly every downstream plan, from staffing and physician compensation to revenue, capital and cash. Yet many organizations plan with one-off spreadsheets that cannot be reused, audited or scenario-tested, budget processes that are lengthy and disconnected from operations, and assumptions that are undocumented or inconsistent. Boards and executives need an integrated, driver-based view of the plan that shows whether it is affordable, how it responds to change and how it will be managed through the year.
This offering sits in the Manage stage of the Cleveland Clinic Healthcare Financial Advisory Lifecycle, which follows an organization's financial decisions through five stages: Plan, Measure, Optimize, Manage and Transform. The Manage stage covers planning, budgeting and forecasting with confidence, and answers the client question "How do we improve planning and decision-making?" name: eClinical Review
tagline: Written opinions from Cleveland Clinic specialists on your physicians' most complex cases, typically within three days.
need:
Physicians regularly face complex or uncommon cases where a subspecialist's view would confirm or change the plan of care. Sending the patient abroad for a second opinion is costly and disruptive, and informal advice from colleagues is hard to obtain, document or act on. Hospitals need a reliable, documented way for their physicians to consult a subspecialist while the patient stays in local care.
It is typically requested by hospitals that want to extend the expertise available to their physicians, add confidence to difficult treatment decisions and build their clinicians' skills one case at a time.
value:

The patient stays with their local physician, who remains responsible for care. Each written report sets out the specialist's assessment and recommendations, so every review also builds the requesting physician's knowledge for similar cases.
